title: The Beijing Hall Built With Zero Nails — Temple of Heaven | China Travel Expert
description:
On Beijing's 7.8km central axis stands a 38-meter wooden hall built without a single nail.

It's the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at the Temple of Heaven, finished in 1420. Inside, 28 wooden columns carry the whole roof with no crossbeam — 4 for the seasons, 12 for the months, 12 for the old two-hour "hours" of the day. The round roof stands for heaven, the square base for earth. Once a year the emperor came here to pray for a good harvest. The complex has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998. This is stop 2 on my walk up the Beijing Central Axis.

🧭 Expert Tip: At the Circular Mound Altar, stand on the round center stone and speak — the tiered marble bounces your voice back so it sounds amplified from below.

中轴线上，一座38米高的大殿，全木无一根钉。
